business: UniDash (working name): a never-miss-a-deadline feed for students, paid for by the university
target: People who approve student-facing software at Indian private universities and autonomous colleges
where: India, private universities and autonomous colleges, starting in Hyderabad

segments.name: IT head / CIO of a private university or college
Dean of students or academic dean
Director, principal or trustee of a private college

behaviours.name: Happy with the current ERP vendor
behaviours.how: Bought the college ERP years ago and expects new features to come from that vendor.

behaviours.name: Budget guardian
behaviours.how: Every new spend needs a committee or trustee approval and a clear reason.

behaviours.name: Rankings and accreditation chaser
behaviours.how: Buys things that help NAAC/NIRF scores and look good to applicants.

behaviours.name: Data and security cautious
behaviours.how: Worries about student data leaks and outside apps touching Microsoft 365.

behaviours.name: Wants proof first
behaviours.how: Asks which other colleges use it and wants to speak to them.

behaviours.name: Overloaded, ignores vendors
behaviours.how: Gets many vendor pitches a week and answers almost none.

objections: Our ERP already has a student app
Students already get every notice on WhatsApp groups
Will my staff have to enter everything a second time?
Student data privacy and the DPDP Act
A tiny new startup: will it still exist next year?
There is no budget left this academic year
IT will not give an outside app access to our Microsoft 365
habits: vendor purchases are approved after a committee meeting
your college uses Microsoft 365 for staff and student email
class notices mostly go out through WhatsApp groups run by faculty
a NAAC accreditation visit is due next year
students complain every semester that they missed an exam notice
